description: Creates a calendar of every club in a league by its code, such as f1, and answers with its links. For Formula 1 that is every Grand Prix's race, or every session of each weekend (practice, qualifying, sprint and race) when weekend is true. Name teams to follow only them, and drivers by slug to follow them too: each session then carries their lines and, once classified, their places. Its feed is the .ics address a calendar app subscribes to, and it stays up to date as sessions are scheduled or moved. Fails for a league of more than 25 clubs, such as the NFL; pick its teams with create_composed_calendar instead.

code.description: The league's code, in any case.

drivers.description: The drivers to follow, by slug (lewis-hamilton); none follows no driver.

teams.description: The league's teams to follow; none follows no team of a series, and every club of any other league.

weekend.description: Whether the calendar takes every session of a racing weekend (practice, qualifying, sprints) rather than the race alone.

name: create_league_calendar

subscribe.description: The whole addresses a person subscribes with, one for each calendar app, and what an assistant tells them.

appleUrl.description: The one-click link for Apple Calendar, on a Mac, iPhone or iPad: the feed's webcal address.

directions.description: What each link is for and why clicking one is safe, for an assistant to pass on to the person.

feedUrl.description: The feed's whole https address, for any other calendar app's "subscribe by URL".

googleUrl.description: The one-click link for Google Calendar. It opens Google Calendar with the feed ready to add, and the person confirms there. The only way into Google Calendar: Google offers an app no way to subscribe someone to a feed.

manageUrl.description: The page where the person changes the calendar's teams and settings later.

outlookUrl.description: The one-click link for Outlook on the web.

title: Create a calendar of a whole league
